verses.20:2: Senhor, no vosso {virtus2} se alegrará o rei: * e {super} a vossa salvação exultará {vehementer}.
verses.20:3: Destes-lhe o desejo do seu coração: * e não o {fraudasti} da vontade dos seus lábios.
verses.20:4: Porque {praevenisti} com bênçãos de doçura: * pusestes na sua cabeça uma coroa de pedra preciosa.
verses.20:6: Grande é a sua glória na vossa salvação: * {o6}.
verses.20:7: Porque pelos séculos dos séculos {dabis}: * o alegrareis {gaudio} com o vosso rosto.
verses.20:8: Porque o rei espera no Senhor: * e na misericórdia do Altíssimo não será abalado.
verses.20:10: {a10}: * o Senhor na sua ira os perturbará, e o fogo os devorará.
verses.20:11: {a11} da terra o seu fruto: * e {semen} dentre os filhos dos homens.

decisions.latin: Inveniátur manus tua ómnibus inimícis tuis … in témpore vultus tui: Dóminus in ira sua … perdes … in te … pones … in relíquiis tuis præparábis
decisions.why: Who is 'tu' in 20:9–13? 20:2–7 speak to the Lord about the king ('eum'); 20:8 speaks of both in the third person; 20:14 speaks to the Lord again ('Exaltáre, Dómine, in virtúte tua', the words of 20:2). Between them, 20:10 names 'Dóminus in ira sua' in the third person right after 'vultus tui' — which reads most easily as said to the king, and that is how many read the Hebrew; but the psalter shifts person inside a verse without warning (15:5 'Dóminus … tu es qui restítues'), and 20:12 'declinavérunt in te mala' and 20:14's return to 'Dómine' read as said to God. The Latin's 'tu' covers both; the Portuguese cannot, because God is vós and a single human addressee is tu (decided). Ruling: vós. (1) It keeps the openness: 'vós' can be God, and it can still be the king — a king has been addressed as vós in Portuguese; 'tu' would exclude God and so resolve what the Latin leaves open. (2) The psalm then speaks to one addressee from 20:9 to 20:14 without a break, and 20:14's 'Exaltai-vos' closes what 20:9 opened. (3) Where the praying voice may be turning to Christ the King, D17 notes that D1 leans to vós. Cost: the reading 'these verses are the people's wish for the king' is not signalled; the 'tu' forms are all written and one touch away. Douay-Rheims 'thy' throughout (no help); Matos Soares 1932 'tu' for God and man alike (no help). Heard (draft 1): the blind reader took 20:9 as said to the Lord and, at 20:10, kept ‘vós’ as the Lord «embora a mudança para o Senhor possa causar dúvida» — the doubt the Latin itself raises; no reader asked for the tu reading.

options.label: vós (God, or the king left open)

forms.a9a: Que a vossa mão {inveniatur9a} por todos os vossos inimigos
forms.a9b: a vossa direita {inveniat9b} todos os que vos odeiam
forms.a10: Vós os fareis como um forno de fogo no tempo do vosso rosto

options.note: Ruling: one addressee from 20:9 to 20:14, as the Latin's 'tu' allows; God first heard, the king not excluded.

options.label: tu (the king)

forms.a9a: Que a tua mão {inveniatur9a} por todos os teus inimigos
forms.a9b: a tua direita {inveniat9b} todos os que te odeiam
forms.a10: Tu os farás como um forno de fogo no tempo do teu rosto

options.note: The reading that makes 20:10's 'Dóminus' a third party: the people speak to the king, as in Ps 19. Decides what the Latin leaves open.

decisions.latin: Dómine, in virtúte tua … Exaltáre, Dómine, in virtúte tua
decisions.why: virtus (δύναμις) → poder (glossary, open; 'in virtúte tua' 53:3; 17:33, 40). The psalm opens and closes on the same words 'Dómine, in virtúte tua', and 20:14 adds 'virtútes tuas' (see decision virtutes): one word three times, as the Latin. Douay-Rheims 'strength'; Matos Soares 1932 'fortaleza … poder' (varies).

options.label: poder
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's word, the inclusio kept.

options.label: força
options.note: Douay-Rheims' 'strength'; 'força' is fortitúdo's (glossary).

decisions.latin: et super salutáre tuum exsultábit
decisions.why: exsultáre super + accusative: 'exult at / over your salvation' (ἐπὶ τῷ σωτηρίῳ σου). The psalm also has 'in salutári tuo' (20:6 → 'na vossa salvação'), so the two prepositions are kept apart. salutáre → salvação (D6); exsultáre → exultar (glossary). Douay-Rheims 'in thy salvation'; Matos Soares 1932 'pela salvação que lhe enviaste' (adds).

options.label: com
options.note: Ruling: 'exultar com' — what one rejoices at; apart from 20:6 'na'.

options.label: pela
options.note: Causal, Matos Soares 1932's preposition (without his addition).

options.label: na
options.note: Douay-Rheims' 'in'; merges super with 20:6's in.

decisions.latin: exsultábit veheménter
decisions.why: valde / veheménter → muito (glossary, open: merged on the Greek σφόδρα, which is the Greek here too; the row names 20:2 as a place that 'may want grandemente locally'). Douay-Rheims 'exceedingly'; Matos Soares 1932 'em extremo'.

options.label: muito
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's word; the verse ends on a paroxytone.

options.label: grandemente
options.note: The row's local alternative; heavier, and the ear found it heavy in Ps 6.

decisions.latin: et voluntáte labiórum ejus non fraudásti eum
decisions.why: fraudáre + ablative: 'to cheat, defraud (someone) of' (the Greek οὐκ ἐστέρησας, 'you did not deprive him'). The other place, 77:29 'non sunt fraudáti a desidério suo' (grep), is the same sense, and 'privar' serves it ('não foram privados do seu desejo'). volúntas → vontade (glossary). Douay-Rheims 'hast not withholden from him the will of his lips'; Matos Soares 1932 'não o defraudaste no pedido que fez com os seus lábios' (explains the will as a request).

options.label: privastes
options.note: Ruling: deprive of — the Latin's and the Greek's sense in a plain verb.

options.label: defraudastes
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's cognate; in Brazil a financial fraud.

decisions.latin: Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis
decisions.why: prævenire with a person as object and a friendly sense — the case the glossary left open (row prævenire: 'the transitive use with a person … 20:4 prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus … will want vir ao encontro de or the like'; 17:19's hostile 'surpreender' does not serve). The Greek προέφθασας, 'you came first to him'. The cognate 'prevenir' is 'warn / prevent' in Brazil. dulcédo → doçura (DRB 'blessings of sweetness'); 30:20 multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ, 67:11 in dulcédine tua (grep). Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, minor — «A tradução não conserva a ideia de antecipação expressa pelo verbo» → ‘vos antecipastes a ele’. Taken in substance with the glossary’s own verb for prævenire (118:147–148 ‘Adiantei-me’), so that the psalter keeps one verb for the Latin one; ‘antecipar’ stays anticipáre’s (76:5, 78:8 ut cito anticípent nos misericórdiæ tuæ). The blind reader did not stop at the line.

options.label: vos adiantastes a ele
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the anticipation kept (the Latinist), in prævenire’s verb in this psalter (118:147–148); God is first with his blessings — the ‘prevenient’ sense, said in plain Portuguese.

options.label: viestes ao encontro dele
options.note: Draft 1. the glossary's candidate; says the going-out to meet, the 'before' only by implication.

options.label: o precedestes
options.note: 'went before him' — the prefix kept; 'preceder' is heard as order in a list.

options.label: o prevenistes
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's cognate: 'you warned him' in Brazil — refused.

options.label: vos antecipastes a ele
options.note: The Latinist’s words; ‘antecipar’ is left to anticipáre (76:5, 78:8).

decisions.latin: longitúdinem diérum
decisions.why: longitúdo diérum: 4 lines (grep: 20:5, 22:6, 90:16, 92:5). Ps 90:16 already has 'Eu o encherei de longos dias' — the noun made an adjective (grammar); followed. in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi → 'para sempre, e pelos séculos dos séculos' (glossary formula, as 9:6). Douay-Rheims 'length of days'; Matos Soares 1932 'largos dias'. Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, minor — the plural ‘pelos séculos dos séculos’ for the singular (→ ‘pelo século do século’) — refused: settled in D27. The stylist — «O final proparoxítono deixa duas sílabas átonas depois do apoio da voz» → ‘e lhe destes, para sempre e pelos séculos dos séculos, longos dias’. Refused, kept as an option: the Latin itself ends on sǽculi, the formula ends a verse wherever it stands in the psalter (9:6), and his line holds the object back behind a parenthesis of nine syllables.

options.label: longos dias
options.note: Ruling: as Ps 90:16.

options.label: longura de dias
options.note: The noun kept (option in Ps 90:16); 'longura' is little said.

decisions.latin: et tribuísti ei longitúdinem diérum in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi
decisions.why: The stylist asked for the formula inside the colon so that the verse does not end on the proparoxytone ‘séculos’. Refused: the Latin ends on sǽculi too, and the formula (D27) closes verses throughout the psalter; the parenthesis holds ‘longos dias’ back nine syllables.

options.label: e lhe destes … para sempre, e pelos séculos dos séculos

forms.o5: e lhe destes {longitudo} para sempre, e pelos séculos dos séculos

options.note: Ruling: the Latin’s order.

options.label: e lhe destes, para sempre e pelos séculos dos séculos, …

forms.o5: e lhe destes, para sempre e pelos séculos dos séculos, {longitudo}

options.note: The stylist’s line: the verse ends on ‘dias’.

decisions.latin: glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum
decisions.why: decor: 'comeliness, grace, beauty, splendour' (Lewis & Short); the Greek here is μεγαλοπρέπειαν (magnificéntia's Greek elsewhere), but the Latin has decor and is followed. 8 lines (grep): 25:8 decórem domus tuæ, 29:8, 44:12, 49:1 spécies decóris ejus, 92:1a decórem indútus est, 103:1 Confessiónem et decórem induísti (twin of 95:6 conféssio et pulchritúdo — so decor must stay apart from pulchritúdo, 'beleza'), 146:1 decóra laudátio. 'decoro' is propriety in Portuguese. Douay-Rheims 'great beauty'; Matos Soares 1932 'grande esplendor'.

options.label: esplendor
options.note: Ruling: Matos Soares 1932's word; serves the robe of 92:1a and 103:1 ('revestiu-se de esplendor'), and leaves 'beleza' to pulchritúdo.

options.label: beleza
options.note: Douay-Rheims' 'beauty'; the plainer word, but pulchritúdo's (95:6).

options.label: formosura
options.note: Beauty of form; spécies (49:1 spécies decóris) will want it.

decisions.latin: glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum
decisions.why: Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «O objeto anteposto retarda o verbo e faz ouvir a construção latina. A ordem direta conserva a imagem e dá mais firmeza ao final» → ‘poreis sobre ele glória e grande esplendor’. Taken: order only (D2). What is lost: the Latin fronts ‘glóriam’ against the first colon’s ‘glória’ (a chiasmus); the two still stand in one verse.

options.label: poreis sobre ele glória e grande …

forms.o6: poreis sobre ele glória e grande {decor}

options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist’s direct order; the verse ends on the oxytone ‘esplendor’.

options.label: glória e grande … poreis sobre ele

forms.o6: glória e grande {decor} poreis sobre ele

options.note: Draft 1: the Latin’s order, the object first.

decisions.latin: Quóniam dabis eum in benedictiónem in sǽculum sǽculi
decisions.why: 'You will give him for a blessing' — the Latin makes the king a blessing (eum in benedictiónem), where the Greek gives blessing to him (δώσεις αὐτῷ εὐλογίαν); the Latin is followed. in sǽculum sǽculi → pelos séculos dos séculos (D27). Douay-Rheims 'thou shalt give him to be a blessing for ever and ever'; Matos Soares 1932 'farás dele uma fonte de bênçãos perpétuas' (adds 'fonte'). Heard (draft 1): the blind reader heard ‘o dareis como bênção’ FIRST as «Concedereis bênçãos ao próprio rei» — the Greek’s dative, which the Latin does not have: a wrong first hearing. Taken: ‘fareis dele uma bênção’ (Douay-Rheims’ sense, ‘give him to be a blessing’), where the king can only be the blessing. The cost: dare becomes ‘fazer’. The stylist — «“Séculos” termina a primeira metade com duas sílabas depois da tônica» → ‘Porque pelos séculos dos séculos o dareis como bênção’: his order taken (order only; the mediant on ‘bênção’). The Latinist’s minor on the plural ‘séculos’ refused (D27).

options.label: fareis dele uma bênção
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the king made a blessing, which the blind reader could not hear in ‘o dareis como bênção’; the stylist’s order, so that the mediant falls on ‘bênção’.

options.label: o dareis como bênção
options.note: Draft 1. dare kept, 'in' + accusative as 'como' (the purpose-predicate).

options.label: lhe dareis a bênção
options.note: The Greek's dative — refused (rule 1).

decisions.latin: lætificábis eum in gáudio cum vultu tuo
decisions.why: lætificáre → alegrar (the verb of lætítia → alegria, glossary). gáudium is another word (χαρά; lætítia is εὐφροσύνη), and 50:10 'dabis gáudium et lætítiam' sets the two side by side, so it cannot be 'alegria' (and 'alegrareis … na alegria' would add an echo the Latin does not have). 4 lines (grep: 20:7, 29:12, 50:10, 125:2a). cum vultu tuo → 'com o vosso rosto', the words of 15:11 (adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo). Douay-Rheims 'make him joyful in gladness with thy countenance'; Matos Soares 1932 'enchê-lo-ás de alegria, mostrando-lhe o teu rosto' (explains). Heard (draft 1): the blind reader listed ‘júbilo’ as unknown (and understood the verse). Kept: the other two candidates fail (see options); for the glossary row gáudium.

options.label: de júbilo
options.note: Ruling: a second joy-word, current and prayable. Cost: júbilo is the noun of jubiláre (13 lines, 46:6 'Ascéndit Deus in júbilo') — see the open glossary row gáudium.

options.label: com gozo
options.note: The older pair 'gozo e alegria'; in Brazil 'gozo' is also sexual pleasure and mockery.

options.label: na alegria
options.note: Douay-Rheims' plain noun; lætítia's word, and an echo of 'alegrareis'.

decisions.latin: Inveniátur manus tua … déxtera tua invéniat
decisions.why: One verb twice, passive then active (εὑρεθείη … εὕροι): kept as one verb. ómnibus inimícis tuis is a dative with the passive, taken as the agent (Douay-Rheims 'by all thy enemies'). odísse → odiar (glossary). Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «A abertura soa como uma determinação formal. Um “que” torna mais natural a súplica, sem desfazer a passiva» → ‘Que a vossa mão seja encontrada por todos os vossos inimigos’. Taken (order and the particle of wish; the passive and the verb kept). The blind reader heard the hand reaching the enemies, by the pull of the second colon — the sense.

options.label: encontrar
options.note: Ruling: the plain verb for finding someone out.

options.label: achar
options.note: Shorter (the colon is long); 'achar' is also 'think'.

decisions.latin: Fructum eórum … et semen eórum a fíliis hóminum
decisions.why: semen (offspring) → descendência (glossary, open, 'for Gustavo's ear'; 17:51). Here the Latin pairs fruit and seed — the strongest case in the psalter so far for keeping 'semente', since 'fruto' is kept and the two images answer each other. pérdere → fazer perecer (D24; the row names 20:11). a fíliis hóminum → 'dentre os filhos dos homens'. Douay-Rheims 'their seed'; Matos Soares 1932 'a sua descendência'.

options.label: a sua descendência
options.note: Ruling: the glossary row, held until it is ruled.

options.label: a sua semente
options.note: Douay-Rheims' 'seed': the image, answering 'o seu fruto' — the row's option, strongest here.

decisions.latin: Quóniam declinavérunt in te mala
decisions.why: declináre with an object: 'they turned (bent) evils against you' (ἔκλιναν εἰς σὲ κακά). Absolute declináre is 'desviar-se' (13:3a 'Todos se desviaram'); 'desviar' with an object is the same verb transitive. 'voltar' is convértere's, 'inclinar' inclináre's (inclína aurem). Douay-Rheims 'they have intended evils against thee' (interprets); Matos Soares 1932 'urdiram contra ti males' (interprets). Heard (draft 1): the stylist’s worst line — «“Desviar contra” combina movimentos que não se encaixam espontaneamente em português; o ouvido espera “desviar de”» → ‘voltaram males contra vós’; the blind reader heard ‘directed evils against you’ by context, and ‘warded off evils’ second. Taken: the turning is kept, and declináre with an object meets convértere nowhere in this psalm. Cost: ‘voltar’ is convértere’s verb elsewhere.

options.label: voltaram males
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist’s verb — the plainest ‘turn against’.

options.label: desviaram males
options.note: Draft 1. declináre's verb (13:3a), transitive; the evils turned from their course onto the addressee.

options.label: tramaram males
options.note: Douay-Rheims / Matos Soares 1932's sense ('intended', 'urdiram'): the verb explained.

decisions.latin: cogitavérunt consília, quæ non potuérunt stabilíre
decisions.why: cogitáre → pensar em (glossary); consílium: in Ps 19:5 the Latinist and the blind reader both refused ‘conselho(s)’ for a person’s plan (advice was heard), and that verse took ‘desígnio’. Here the blind reader heard ‘pensaram conselhos’ FIRST as «recomendações ou orientações» and the stylist found the pair not current («parece falar de recomendações pensadas») → ‘pensaram em planos que não puderam firmar’. Taken with Ps 19’s noun, so that the king’s ‘desígnio’ confirmed (19:5) and the enemies’ ‘desígnios’ not made firm (20:12) answer each other as the Latin’s consílium … consília do. stabilíre → firmar (glossary statúere, open).

options.label: pensaram em desígnios
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist’s build (‘pensar em’, the glossary’s cogitáre) with Ps 19:5’s noun.

options.label: pensaram em planos
options.note: The stylist’s line: the plainer noun.

options.label: pensaram conselhos
options.note: Draft 1: the glossary noun; heard as advice.

decisions.latin: Quóniam pones eos dorsum
decisions.why: 'You will make them a back' — a double accusative, the Greek θήσεις αὐτοὺς νῶτον: they will turn their backs, in flight. The glossary row dare dorsum (Ps 17:41 'E me destes as costas dos meus inimigos') says 20:13 will want the same image; pónere + predicate → the Portuguese build (glossary: fazer … como, 17:35). 'pôr de costas' would lay them on their backs. Douay-Rheims 'thou shalt make them turn their back'; Matos Soares 1932 'os porás em fuga' (explains). Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, MAJOR — «“Dorsum” é predicativo de “eos”: fareis deles um dorso. “Dar as costas” explica a imagem como uma ação, resolvendo a expressão peculiar do latim» → ‘fareis deles um dorso’; the blind reader heard ‘fareis os inimigos fugir’ first. Taken in substance: the predicate is kept as a state, with the copula Portuguese needs (D2) — ‘os fareis ficar de costas’, ‘you will make them be backs-turned’ — and ‘costas’, the Portuguese back (‘dorso’ is an animal’s or a book’s). ‘dar’, which the Latin does not have, is gone.

options.label: ficar de costas
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the predicate as a state (the Latinist), the copula ‘ficar’ supplied; the back kept.

options.label: dar as costas
options.note: Draft 1. 'fazer dar as costas' — the back kept, and the idiom of 17:41.

options.label: voltar as costas
options.note: Douay-Rheims' 'turn their back'; 'voltar' is convértere's.

options.label: pôr em fuga
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the image explained — refused (rule 2).

options.label: fareis deles um dorso
options.note: The Latinist’s line: ‘fazer de X Y’ is the glossary build for pónere + predicate (17:12); ‘dorso’ is an animal’s or a book’s back in Portuguese, not a man’s.

decisions.latin: in relíquiis tuis præparábis vultum eórum
decisions.why: An obscure colon, the Greek word for word (ἐν τοῖς περιλοίποις σου ἑτοιμάσεις τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν): 'in your remnants you will prepare their face'. Matos Soares 1932 supplies arrows in a gloss ('prepararás o seu rosto para (receber as setas) que te restam'); Douay-Rheims 'in thy remnants'. Kept as open as the Latin. relíquiæ (36:37–38 'relíquiæ hómini pacífico … relíquiæ impiórum') is what is left over, a remnant.

options.label: nos vossos restos
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's words, nothing supplied.

options.label: com o que vos resta
options.note: The ablative as instrument, a clause for the noun (Matos Soares 1932's sense without the arrows).

decisions.latin: cantábimus et psallémus virtútes tuas
decisions.why: psállere → entoar salmos (D25; the glossary names 20:14 as a place where psállere stands beside cantáre, so it cannot be 'cantar'). virtútes tuas, plural (Greek τὰς δυναστείας σου, 'your mighty acts' — the Greek of 19:7b potentátibus): the object of both verbs. 'entoar salmos' takes a dative (7:18 'ao nome'), so the object is said 'ao vosso poder'. The plural 'poderes' is heard as a set of faculties or super-powers; Douay-Rheims makes it singular ('thy power'), and the singular closes the psalm on the word of 20:2 and 20:14a. Heard (draft 1): the Latinist, MAJOR — «“Virtutes” está no plural e designa o conteúdo celebrado pelos dois verbos. A tradução o reduz ao poder singular e o apresenta como destinatário dos salmos» → ‘cantaremos e celebraremos em salmos as vossas forças’. Taken in substance: the plural back, and the accusative — ‘entoar em salmos’ keeps D25’s two words (entoar … salmos) while taking a direct object; ‘forças’ refused (força is fortitúdo’s), ‘celebrar’ refused (D25). The stylist — «A mesma palavra nos dois pousos produz um eco excessivamente marcado» → ‘Senhor, no vosso poder, exaltai-vos’: refused, kept as an option — the echo is the Latin’s own (in virtúte tua … virtútes tuas, at the same two cadences; rule 5’s exception), and ‘Exaltai-vos’ opens the formula of 56:6, 56:12, 107:6.

options.label: e entoaremos em salmos os vossos poderes

forms.virtutes: e entoaremos em salmos os vossos poderes

options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the Latin’s plural and its accusative; ‘poderes’ can also serve the plural virtútes of 102:21, 148:2 (the Powers who praise).

options.label: ao vosso poder

forms.virtutes: e entoaremos salmos ao vosso poder

options.note: Draft 1. Douay-Rheims' singular; the psalm's word three times.

options.label: aos vossos poderes

forms.virtutes: e entoaremos salmos aos vossos poderes

options.note: The Latin's number.

options.label: às vossas maravilhas

forms.virtutes: e entoaremos salmos às vossas maravilhas

options.note: Matos Soares 1932: mirabília's word — refused.

options.label: e celebraremos em salmos as vossas forças

forms.virtutes: e celebraremos em salmos as vossas forças

options.note: The Latinist’s line: ‘celebrar’ is not D25’s verb, ‘força’ is fortitúdo’s.

decisions.latin: Exaltáre, Dómine, in virtúte tua
decisions.why: Glossary: Exaltáre → exaltai-vos (open; the row names 20:14). The stylist asked to move the imperative to the mediant, to break the echo poder … poder(es). Refused: the echo is the Latin’s own, and the imperative heads the formula wherever it stands (56:6, 56:12, 93:2, 107:6).

options.label: Exaltai-vos, Senhor, no vosso poder
options.note: Ruling: the Latin’s order.

options.label: Senhor, no vosso poder, exaltai-vos
options.note: The stylist’s line: the mediant on the imperative.

choices.20:2: The Latin's order kept (the vocative, the means, then the king); natural in Portuguese.
choices.20:3: Desidérium cordis ejus tribuísti ei: the Latin fronts the object; Portuguese says the verb first ('Destes-lhe'). tríbuere → dar (glossary row bona tríbuere; 15:7).
choices.20:4: posuísti in cápite ejus → 'pusestes na sua cabeça' ('na' for in, keeping 'sobre' for super); de lápide pretióso → 'de pedra preciosa', the Latin's singular (Douay-Rheims makes it plural).
choices.20:5: pétere → pedir (glossary postuláre shares it). 'Pediu-vos vida' — no article, as the Latin's bare vitam (the thing asked, not 'his life').
choices.20:6: in salutári tuo → 'na vossa salvação' (D6); impónere super → 'pôr sobre' (super (place) → sobre, glossary).
choices.20:8: commovéri → ser abalado (glossary, with 14:5b and 15:8; one Greek verb, σαλεύω). sperat in → 'espera no' (glossary speráre in → esperar em).
choices.20:10: pónere + predicate → 'fazer … como' (glossary; 17:35). in témpore vultus tui → 'no tempo do vosso rosto' (vultus → rosto, glossary): the Latin's image of the face's appearing, not explained (Douay-Rheims 'in the time of thy anger' and Matos Soares 1932 explain it). conturbáre → perturbar (glossary). 'perturbará … devorará' rhyme inside a colon, not at a cadence.
choices.20:11: pérdere → fazer perecer (D24; the row names 20:11). de terra → 'da terra'.
choices.20:12: cogitáre → pensar (glossary; with an object, 'pensar' + noun); consília → 'conselhos' (glossary consílium), answering 19:5 'confirme todos os teus conselhos'; stabilíre (only here and the noun 103:5, grep) → 'firmar', the glossary's proposal for statúere — the enemies' counsels are not made firm, the king's are confirmed.
choices.20:14: Exaltáre → 'Exaltai-vos' (glossary row Exaltáre, which names 20:14). The psalm ends on 'poder' as it began.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm20.txt, thirteen prayed verses with DO's ids (20:2–20:14). No titulus (D7). No Diurnal Monástico for this psalm in the parallels.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps020.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932 raw text). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: gáudium (4), jubil- (13), lætificáre (8), decor (8), fraudáre (2), dulcédo (3), clíbanus (1), relíqui- (relíquiæ 4 of 12 lines), stabil- (2), longitúdo (4), prævenire (7). Latin readings kept against the Hebrew: 20:4 'bênçãos de doçura … coroa de pedra preciosa', 20:7 'o dareis como bênção' (and against the Greek's dative), 20:10 'no tempo do vosso rosto', 20:12 'desviaram males contra vós', 20:13 'nos vossos restos preparareis o rosto deles' (the Hebrew has bowstrings), 20:14 'entoaremos salmos'. 16 decisions. Vós imperative: 'Exaltai-vos' (safe).

Draft 1: hard pass. Soft flags accepted: 20:3 −3 / −3 (the Latin's long words; nothing dropped); 20:5 second colon −5 (longitúdinem diérum → 'longos dias', as 90:16); 20:7 first colon −3; 20:11 second colon +3 ('descendência' for semen); 20:12 second colon −6 ('firmar' for stabilíre); 20:14 second colon +5 (psállere → 'entoar salmos', D25's two words, and the dative 'ao vosso poder'). Rhyme flag 20:14 'poder … poder' — the Latin's own echo (in virtúte tua … virtútes tuas), kept.

Draft 1. Two majors (20:13, 20:14) and three minors (20:4; 20:5 and 20:7, the plural of séculos); the marks confirmed. «A tradução conserva em geral o sentido e as imagens do latim, mas explica a construção peculiar de 20:13 e altera o número e a função de “virtutes” em 20:14.» Passed the address of 20:9–13 (vós), 'no tempo do vosso rosto', 'desviaram males', 'nos vossos restos'.

outcomes.remark: minor: 'viestes ao encontro dele' loses the anticipation of prævenísti → 'vos antecipastes a ele'
outcomes.reason: Taken in substance with prævenire's verb in this psalter (118:147–148 'adiantar-se'); his 'antecipar' is anticipáre's and is an option.

outcomes.remark: minor: 'pelos séculos dos séculos' pluralizes the singular → 'pelo século do século'
outcomes.reason: Settled in D27: the plural is how the phrase lives in Portuguese; number is grammar.

outcomes.remark: minor: the same plural
MAJOR: dorsum is a predicate of eos; 'dar as costas' explains it as an action → 'fareis deles um dorso'
outcomes.reason: Taken in substance: the predicate kept as a state with the copula 'ficar' ('os fareis ficar de costas'); 'costas' is the human back ('dorso' is an animal's or a book's). His line is an option.

outcomes.remark: MAJOR: virtútes is plural and the content sung by both verbs; 'ao vosso poder' makes it singular and the addressee → 'cantaremos e celebraremos em salmos as vossas forças'
outcomes.reason: Plural and accusative restored: 'e entoaremos em salmos os vossos poderes' (D25's words, a direct object); 'celebrar' and 'forças' refused (D25; força is fortitúdo's). His line is an option.

audit.note: Draft 1. Six verses, seven remarks; best 20:8, worst 20:12. «O salmo tem sobriedade e, em geral, cabe bem na voz; algumas inversões e combinações de palavras ainda fazem ouvir o latim … As imagens difíceis pedem uma recitação pausada, mas sua estranheza não é, por si, defeito da tradução.» Five taken (order, a particle, two word choices), two refused with options.

outcomes.remark: the verse ends on the proparoxytone 'séculos' → 'e lhe destes, para sempre e pelos séculos dos séculos, longos dias'
outcomes.reason: The Latin ends on sǽculi too; the formula closes verses throughout the psalter; his line holds the object behind a nine-syllable parenthesis.

outcomes.remark: the fronted object delays the verb and sounds Latin → 'poreis sobre ele glória e grande esplendor'
outcomes.reason: Order only (D2).

outcomes.remark: 'séculos' at the mediant → 'Porque pelos séculos dos séculos o dareis como bênção'
outcomes.reason: His order taken; the verb changed for the blind reader's sake ('fareis dele uma bênção').

outcomes.remark: 'Seja encontrada' sounds like a formal decree → 'Que a vossa mão seja encontrada por todos os vossos inimigos'
outcomes.reason: The particle of wish and the order; passive and verb kept.

outcomes.remark: 'desviar contra' joins movements that do not fit → 'voltaram males contra vós' (worst line)
outcomes.reason: The turning kept in the plainest verb; declináre with an object meets convértere nowhere here.

outcomes.remark: 'pensaram conselhos' is not current and sounds like advice → 'pensaram em planos'
outcomes.reason: His build taken with Ps 19:5's noun ('desígnios'), so that consílium / consília answer each other across the two psalms; 'planos' is option 2.

outcomes.remark: the same word at both cadences (poder … poder) → 'Senhor, no vosso poder, exaltai-vos'
outcomes.reason: The echo is the Latin's own at the same two cadences (in virtúte tua … virtútes tuas; rule 5's exception), and 'Exaltai-vos' heads its formula everywhere (56:6, 56:12, 93:2, 107:6).

audit.note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. 29 items, 2 unknown words (exultará, júbilo). Two wrong first hearings, both mended: 20:7 'o dareis como bênção' heard as blessings given TO the king (the Greek's reading), 20:12 'pensaram conselhos' heard as advice. The address of 20:9–10 heard as the Lord throughout, with the doubt the Latin itself raises at 20:10. 'dar as costas' heard as flight; 20:13b not understood (nor is the Latin).

outcomes.remark: 'no vosso poder': because of (heard first) / under the Lord's power
outcomes.reason: in virtúte tua holds both.

outcomes.remark: 'a vossa salvação': deliverance / eternal salvation (heard first)
outcomes.reason: D6; salutáre holds both.

outcomes.remark: 'Destes-lhe o desejo do seu coração': granted what he wished (heard first) / put a wish in him
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: 'a vontade dos seus lábios': what he asked in words (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: 'coroa de pedra preciosa': made of / set with (heard first)
outcomes.reason: de lápide pretióso holds both.

outcomes.remark: 'Pediu-vos vida': the king (heard first) / someone unnamed
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: 'longos dias para sempre': a long earthly life / a life without end (heard first)
outcomes.reason: The Latin says both (longitúdinem diérum in sǽculum).

outcomes.remark: 'a sua glória': honour (heard first) / visible splendour
outcomes.reason: glória holds both.

outcomes.remark: 'na vossa salvação': the deliverance / spiritual salvation (heard first)
'o dareis como bênção': make the king a blessing for others / give blessings to the king (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Wrong first hearing — the Greek's dative, not the Latin's eum in benedictiónem → 'fareis dele uma bênção'.

outcomes.remark: 'com o vosso rosto': the sight of it (heard first) / presence, favour
outcomes.reason: As 15:11; cum vultu tuo holds both.

outcomes.remark: 'espera no Senhor': trusts (heard first) / waits
outcomes.reason: speráre in (glossary).

outcomes.remark: 'não será abalado': not lose confidence (heard first) / not be overthrown
outcomes.reason: commovéri holds both.

outcomes.remark: 'vossa mão … vossos inimigos': the Lord's (heard first) / the king's
outcomes.reason: The openness the address decision keeps; heard as the ruling meant.

outcomes.remark: 'Seja encontrada … por todos': the enemies find the hand / the hand reaches them (heard first)
outcomes.reason: The sense of the verse; the passive kept.

outcomes.remark: 'a vossa direita': the right hand (heard first) / the right side
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: 'Vós os fareis … o Senhor': vós is the Lord, then named in the third person (heard first, with doubt) / vós is the king
outcomes.reason: The Latin's own doubt at this verse, kept open under vós; the tu reading is one touch away.

outcomes.remark: 'como um forno de fogo': burn like an oven / suffer inside one (heard first)
outcomes.reason: ut clíbanum ignis holds both.

outcomes.remark: 'no tempo do vosso rosto': when you appear (heard first, unsure) / during your presence
outcomes.reason: The Latin's image, not explained; heard as meant.

outcomes.remark: 'o seu fruto': offspring / crops (heard first)
outcomes.reason: The Latin's image; the second colon turns it to offspring, as the blind reader noted.

outcomes.remark: 'seu fruto … sua descendência': the enemies' (heard first) / the Lord's
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: 'os filhos dos homens': mankind (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: 'desviaram males contra vós': directed evils against you (heard first, by context) / warded them off
outcomes.reason: With the stylist → 'voltaram males contra vós', which has only the first hearing.

outcomes.remark: 'pensaram conselhos': devised plans / thought up advice (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Wrong first hearing → 'pensaram em desígnios' (Ps 19:5's noun).

outcomes.remark: 'não puderam firmar': could not carry out (heard first) / could not establish
outcomes.reason: stabilíre holds both.

outcomes.remark: 'os fareis dar as costas': flee (heard first) / turn away, ignore
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; the wording changed for the Latinist's major ('ficar de costas'), which keeps the flight.

outcomes.remark: 'nos vossos restos': what is left of something yours (heard first, unidentified) / remains of a body
outcomes.reason: The Latin is as obscure; Matos Soares' arrows are a gloss (option 2 is his sense without them).

outcomes.remark: 'preparareis o rosto deles': some preparation of their faces, unclear (heard first) / set their faces in a direction
outcomes.reason: The Latin's words; not explained.

outcomes.remark: 'Exaltai-vos': show your greatness (heard first) / praise yourself / be agitated
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly (glossary Exaltáre → exaltai-vos).

outcomes.remark: unknown word: exultará
outcomes.reason: exsultáre → exultar (glossary, working); listed unknown before (Ps 12), kept.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: júbilo
outcomes.reason: Kept for gáudium: 'alegria' is lætítia's (50:10 has both) and 'gozo' is heard sexually in Brazil; see the open glossary row gáudium.

audit.note: v2. Nine verses changed against draft 1: 20:4 'vos adiantastes a ele' (Latinist, minor); 20:6 direct order (stylist); 20:7 'Porque pelos séculos dos séculos fareis dele uma bênção' (the blind reader heard the Greek's dative; the stylist's order); 20:9 'Que a vossa mão seja encontrada' (stylist); 20:12 'voltaram males … pensaram em desígnios' (the stylist's worst line, the blind reader's 'advice'); 20:13 'os fareis ficar de costas' (Latinist, MAJOR); 20:14 'e entoaremos em salmos os vossos poderes' (Latinist, MAJOR). New decisions for refused stylist lines kept selectable: longitudo_order (20:5), order6 (20:6), consilia (20:12), exaltare (20:14). Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json, the file the three v1 critics read). Script: ps020/revise_v2.py; ps020/validate.py (a copy of ps017's slot checker taking a folder) passes.

Draft 2: hard pass. Soft flags accepted: 20:3 −3 / −3; 20:4 first colon −3; 20:5 −5; 20:9 first colon +3 ('Que' and the passive); 20:11 +3; 20:12 second colon −5; 20:14 second colon +6 ('entoar em salmos', D25's two words, and the plural). No rhyme flag (the Latin's echo poder … poderes is no longer an identical rhyme).
